saints.name: The Circumcision of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.title: The Circumcision of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.notes: On the eighth day after His Nativity, our Lord Jesus Christ was circumcised in accordance with the Old Testament Law. All male infants underwent circumcision as a sign of God’s Covenant with the holy Forefather Abraham and his descendants [Genesis 17:10-14, Leviticus 12:3]. After this…

saints.name: Basil the Great
saints.title: Saint Basil the Great, Archbishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia
saints.notes: Saint Basil the Great, Archbishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia, “belongs not to the Church of Caesarea alone, nor merely to his own time, nor was he of benefit only to his own kinsmen, but rather to all lands and cities worldwide, and to all people he brought and still brings benefit, and for…

saints.name: Basil of Ancyra
saints.title: Martyr Basil of Ancyra
saints.notes: Saint Basil lived in the time of Julian the Apostate (331-363), and confessed his faith in Christ before the governor Saturninus. He was tortured in Ancyra, then sent to Constantinople, where he was suspended from a tree, stretched on a rack, beaten, then stabbed with red-hot needles. He was also…

saints.name: Emilia
saints.title: Saint Emilia, Mother of Saint Basil the Great
saints.notes: Saint Basil the Great’s mother Saint Emilia was the daughter of a martyr. On the Greek calendar, she is commemorated on May 30. Saint Basil’s father was also named Basil. He was a lawyer and renowned rhetorician, and lived at Caesarea. Ten children were born to the elder Basil and…

saints.name: Icon of the Mother of God “You are a Vineyard”
saints.title: Icon of the Mother of God “You are a Vineyard” (Georgian: Shen khar venakhi)
saints.notes: On the Feast of Saint Basil the Great, we commemorate an Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos known as "You are a Vineyard," because on this day, through her Icon, the Most Holy Theotokos healed an unbelieving man of an incurable disease. After he was healed, he began to believe. Later, the Icon flowed…

saints.name: Monastic Martyr Telemakhos
saints.title: Monastic Martyr Telemakhos
saints.notes: Saint Telemakhos (Telémakhos) was a monk who lived in the V century during the reign of Emperor Honorius. He traveled from Asia to Rome desiring to save the city. He was opposed to the gladiatorial contests which took place in the amphitheaters, and so he rushed to the Colosseum and shouted for…

saints.name: Forefeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.title: Forefeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.notes: The first day of the Forefeast of Theophany falls on January 2. Like the hymns for the Nativity, many of the Church’s hymns of this period are slightly modified versions of the hymns of Holy Week. One of the hymns at Matins today says that the coming Feast of Theophany will be “even…

saints.name: Repose of Venerable Seraphim
saints.title: Repose of Venerable Seraphim, Wonderworker of Sarov
saints.notes: Saint Seraphim of Sarov, a great ascetic of the Russian Church, was born on July 19, 1754. His parents, Isidore and Agathia Moshnin, were inhabitants of Kursk. Isidore was a merchant. Toward the end of his life, he began construction of a cathedral in Kursk, but he died before the completion of the…

saints.name: Sylvester
saints.title: Saint Sylvester, Pope of Rome
saints.notes: Saint Sylvester, Bishop of Rome (314-335) was born at Rome of Christian parents named Rufinus and Justa. His father soon died, and the saint remained in the care of his mother. Sylvester’s teacher, the presbyter Quirinus, gave him a fine education and raised him as a true Christian. When he…

saints.name: Sylvester of the Kiev Near Caves
saints.title: Venerable Sylvester of the Kiev Near Caves
saints.notes: Saint Sylvester of the Caves lived during the twelfth century and was igumen of the Mikhailovsk Vydubitsk monastery at Kiev. He continued the work of Saint Nestor the Chronicler (October 27) and he wrote nine lives of the holy saints of the Kiev Caves. In the service to the Fathers venerated in the…

saints.name: Juliana of Lazarevo
saints.title: Righteous Juliana of Lazarevo, Murom
saints.notes: Righteous Juliana of Lazarevo and Murom presents an astonishing example of a self-denying Russian Christian woman. She was the daughter of the nobleman Justin Nediurev. From her early years she lived devoutly, kept the fasts strictly and set aside much time for prayer. Having been orphaned at an…

saints.name: Theogenes
saints.title: Hieromartyr Theogenes, Bishop of Parium on the Hellespont
saints.notes: The Hieromartyr Theogenes was bishop of the Asia Minor city of Parion at the beginning of the fourth century. During the reign of the emperor Licinius (311-324), a coruler with Constantine the Great, the tribune Zalinkinthius demanded that he give up the priesthood, to renounce Christ and to enlist…

saints.name: New Martyr George of Iberia
saints.title: New Martyr George of Iberia
saints.notes: Saint George (Zorzes) was from Georgia, and was sold into slavery when he was young. His master, a Muslim from the Greek island of Mytilene, forced him to embrace Islam and renamed him Sali. After his master died, George remained on the island and opened a small shop. In 1770, when he was seventy…

saints.name: Forefeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.title: Forefeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.notes: The second day of the Forefeast of Theophany falls on January 3. Today’s hymns invite us to go in spirit to the Jordan River where the Creator comes to be baptized. He is the Light which shines in the darkness (John 1:5), and today He begins to overcome that darkness.

saints.name: Prophet Malachi
saints.title: Holy Prophet Malachi
saints.notes: The Holy Prophet Malachi lived 400 years before the Birth of Christ, at the time of the return of the Jews from the Babylonian Captivity. Malachi was the last of the Old Testament prophets, therefore the holy Fathers call him “the seal of the prophets.” Manifesting himself an image of…

saints.name: Gordius at Caesarea
saints.title: Martyr Gordius at Caesarea, in Cappadocia
saints.notes: The Martyr Gordius was born at the end of the third century in the city of Caesarea of Cappadocia into a Christian family. When he came of age, he entered military service. Because of his valor and military skill, he was made a centurion. During the persecution of Christians at the beginning of the…

saints.name: Genevieve of Paris
saints.title: Venerable Genevieve of Paris
saints.notes: Saint Genevieve (Geneviève) was born of wealthy parents in Gaul (modern France) in the village of Nanterre, near Paris, around 422. Her father’s name was Severus, and her mother was called Gerontia. According to the custom of the time, she often tended her father’s sheep on Mount Valerien.…

saints.name: Euthymius
saints.title: Saint Euthymius (Takaishvili)
saints.notes: Saint Ekvtime (Euthymius) Takaishvili, called the “Man of God,” was born January 3, 1863, in the village of Likhauri, in the Ozurgeti district of Guria, to the noble family of Svimeon Takaishvili and Gituli Nakashidze. He was orphaned at a young age and raised by his uncle. From early…

saints.name: Discovery of the Relics of the Holy Great Martyr Ephraim
saints.title: Discovery of the Relics of the Holy Great Martyr Ephraim
saints.notes: After Saint Ephraim (Ephraίm) suffered martyrdom on May 5,1426, he remained forgotten for nearly 500 years, hidden in the depths of silence and oblivion until January 3, 1950. By then a women’s monastery had sprung up on the site of the old monastery. The Igoumeness Makaria († April 23, 1999)…

saints.name: Forefeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.title: Forefeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.notes: The third day of the Forefeast of Theophany falls on January 4. The hymns compare the Feast of the Nativity with the coming Feast. “There shepherds saw the Child and were amazed; here the voice of the Father proclaims the only-begotten Son.”

saints.name: Synaxis of the Seventy Apostles
saints.title: Synaxis of the Seventy Apostles
saints.notes: The Synaxis of the Seventy Apostles was established by the Orthodox Church to indicate the equal honor of each of the Seventy. They were sent two by two by the Lord Jesus Christ to go before Him into the cities He would visit (Luke 10:1). Besides the celebration of the Synaxis of the Holy…

saints.name: Theoctistus
saints.title: Venerable Theoctistus, Abbot at Cucomo, in Sicily
saints.notes: Saint Theoktistos lived in the second half of the eighth century, during a period of widespread iconoclastic heresy. The Venerable One was the founder and Igoumen of Cucomo Monastery on the island of Sicily. During that difficult time for the Church, the Orthodox were persecuted by iconoclastic…

saints.name: Repose of Saint Eustathius I
saints.title: Repose of Saint Eustathius I, Archbishop of Serbia
saints.notes: Saint Eustathius, Archbishop of Serbia, lived in the second half of the thirteenth century, during the reign of the Serbian king Stephen Urosh (1262-1320). He was born in the diocese of Budim into a pious Christian family, where he received a spiritual upbringing. Distinguished by remarkable…

saints.name: Aquila
saints.title: Saint Aquila, Deacon, of the Kiev Caves
saints.notes: Saint Aquila the Deacon of the Kiev Caves (14th Century), became famous as a great faster, having spent a long while as a hermit. He ate neither vareny (pirogi) nor sweet food, he ate vegetables seldom and only in small quantities. During fasting periods, he ate only a single prosphoron. Those…

saints.name: Confessors Zosimus the Hermit and Athanasius the Commentarisius
saints.title: Confessors Zosimus the Hermit and Athanasius the Commentarisius (Superintendent of Prisoners), Anchorites, of Cilicia
saints.notes: The Monk Confessor Zosimus came from Cilicia and was an inhabitant of the wilderness. During a time of persecution against Christians under the emperor Diocletian (284-305) Saint Zosimus was seized and subjected to fierce torture for the Faith, but by the power of God he was preserved unharmed.…

saints.name: Nikephoros the Leper
saints.title: Saint Nikephoros the Leper
saints.notes: Father Nikephoros (Nikēphóros - Nicholas Tzanakakis in the world) was born in 1890 in a mountainous village in Khania, in Sikari, Kastanohori to the west of the prefecture with a healthy climate, with beautiful forests, rich waters, gorges and caves. This village has a peculiarity that we do not…

saints.name: Euthymius and twelve other Monks
saints.title: Venerable Euthymius and twelve other Monks, martyred at Vatopedi
saints.notes: The Monk Martyr Euthymius, Igumen of the Vatopedi Monastery on Mount Athos, and twelve other monks suffered martyrdom for denouncing the Latinizing Patriarchs Michael Paleologos (1261-1281) and John Bekkos (1275-1282) as heretics. Saint Euthymius was drowned in the sea, and the monks were hanged.

saints.name: New Martyr Onuphrius of Hilandar
saints.title: Venerable New Martyr Onuphrius of Hilandar (Mount Athos)
saints.notes: The New Martyr Onuphrius, in the world Matthew, was born in Bulgaria in Gabrovo in the Trnovo diocese. Matthew became angry with his parents one day, and said he wished to become a Moslem. Unfortunately, he was overheard by the Hagarenes, who wished to take him away. He regretted these words as…

saints.name: Fathers of the Shio-Mgvime Monastery
saints.title: Holy Fathers of the Shio-Mgvime Monastery
saints.notes: The Thirteen Syrian fathers arrived in Georgia in the 6th century, having received a blessing for their journey from the Most Holy Theotokos. They settled on Zedazeni Mountain, living an ascetic life of prayer and fasting. Their spiritual leader, Ioane, then sent them to perform good works…

saints.name: Metropolitan Symeon of Smolensk
saints.title: Metropolitan Symeon of Smolensk
saints.notes: Saint Symeon (Symeón) the future Metropolitan of Smolensk, was born in the city of Tobolsk in Siberia, and was a descendent of theMolyukov family of merchants. His love for the monastic life led him to the Monastery of Saints Boris and Gleb in the city of Rostov. After his tonsure, he remained…

saints.name: Eve of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.title: Eve of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.notes: The fourth day of the Forefeast of Theophany falls on January 5. If January 5th falls on a weekday, the following order is observed: Vespers on the evening of the 4th, then Matins. The First Hour is not read after Matins. On the 5th we read the Royal Hours, followed by Vespers and the Liturgy of…

saints.name: Theopemptus
saints.title: Hieromartyr Theopemptus, Bishop of Nicomedia, and Martyr Theonas
saints.notes: The Holy Martyrs Theopemptus and Theonas suffered in Nicomedia in the year 303. Saint Theopemptus was bishop in Nicomedia in the time of Diocletian. Speaking out against idolatry, he defended the faith in Christ. Because of this, he became one of the first victims of the Diocletian persecution. The…

saints.name: Synkletika of Alexandria
saints.title: Venerable Synkletika of Alexandria
saints.notes: Saint Syncletica (Synklētikḗ) was a native of Alexandria, the daughter of wealthy parents. She was very beautiful, but from a young age she thought only about the things which are pleasing to God. Loving the purity of virginity, she refused to marry anyone, and spent all her time in fasting and…

saints.name: Micah
saints.title: Prophet Micah
saints.notes: The Holy Prophet Micah was a companion of the holy prophet Elias. He prophesied the ruin of King Ahab in a war with the Assyrians, for which he was cast into prison. Set free after the downfall of Ahab (3 Kings 22: 8-22), the holy prophet Micah died as a martyr in the ninth century B.C.

saints.name: Apollinaria of Egypt
saints.title: Saint Apollinaria of Egypt
saints.notes: The renowned Apollinaria (Απολλιναρία) lived during the reign of Leo the Great (‎457–474), and was the daughter of Anthemius, a former proconsul of Rome during the minority of Theodosius the Younger (408-450). Saint Apollinaria was renowned for her beauty and wisdom, as well as for…

saints.name: Phosterius the Hermit
saints.title: Venerable Phosterius the Hermit
saints.notes: Saint Phosterius the Hermit led an ascetical life on a lofty mountain, where he was fed by an angel. He brought many back to the Church from the heresy of Iconoclasm by his miracles and saintly life.

saints.name: Menas of Sinai
saints.title: Venerable Menas of Sinai
saints.notes: Saint Menas lived in asceticism for more than fifty years in the monastery of Sinai, where he died peacefully in the second half of the sixth century. Myrrh flowed from his holy relics. Saint John Climacus speaks of this wonderful man in The Ladder of Divine Ascent (Step 4:34).

saints.name: Gregory of Crete
saints.title: Venerable Gregory of Crete
saints.notes: Saint Gregory of Akrita was born on the island of Crete in the year 760, and was raised by pious parents. At this time the iconoclast heretics persecuted the Orthodox. The youth Gregory, wanting to preserve his Orthodox Faith, went to Seleukia and led a life of piety. At the age of twenty, Saint…

saints.name: Romanus the Martyr
saints.title: Venerable Romanus the Martyr
saints.notes: New Martyr Romanus of Karpenisi was born in Karpenisi in central Greece. He was a monk on Mount Athos for a time, and suffered for Christ at Constantinople, beheaded by the Turks in the year 1694. His relics were taken by ship to England.

saints.name: Feast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.title: Feast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.notes: Theophany is the Feast which reveals the Most Holy Trinity to the world through the Baptism of the Lord (Mt.3:13-17; Mark 1:9-11; Luke 3:21-22). God the Father spoke from Heaven about the Son, the Son was baptized by Saint John the Forerunner, and the Holy Spirit descended upon the Son in the form…

saints.name: Macarius of Mount Athos
saints.title: Venerable Macarius of Mount Athos
saints.notes: Saint Macarius was born in Thessalonica during the reign of Emperor Manuel II Paleologos, and went to Vatopedi Monastery on Mount Athos when he was young. Later, he went to Constantinople and became igumen of the Monastery of the Pantocrator, and chaplain to the Emperor. He died in 1431 during an…

saints.name: Afterfeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.title: Afterfeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.notes: On the first day of the Afterfeast of Theophany, the Church extols Saint John the Baptist as the greatest man born of a woman. He surpasses all the ancient prophets because he baptized the Messiah, Whose coming he foretold.

saints.name: Synaxis of the Holy Glorious Prophet
saints.title: Synaxis of the Holy Glorious Prophet, Forerunner and Baptist John
saints.notes: In the Orthodox Church it is customary, on the day following the Great Feasts of the Lord and the Mother of God, to remember those saints who participated directly in the sacred event. So, on the day following the Theophany of the Lord, the Church honors the one who participated directly in the…

saints.name: Pakhomios of Keno Lake
saints.title: Saint Pakhomios of Keno Lake
saints.notes: Saint Pakhomios is commemorated on the Saturday after Theophany. He was the disciple and fellow ascetic of Saint Alexander of Oshevensk (April 20). Father Pakhomios left his instructor's Monastery shortly after the latter's repose. A strict faster and man of prayer, Pakhomios spent many years in…

saints.name: Brannock of Braunton
saints.title: Saint Brannock of Braunton
saints.notes: Saint Brannock lived in the sixth century, and tutored the children of the Welsh ruler Brychan. He went with King Brychan on a pilgrimage to venerate the tombs of the Apostles. On the way home, he stopped in Brittany and remained there several years. Eventually, the saint settled in Braunton,…

saints.name: Cedd of Lastingham
saints.title: Saint Cedd of Lastingham
saints.notes: Saint Cedd was a missionary and bishop who spread the faith throughout England during the seventh century. The eldest of four brothers, all of whom became priests, he was born in 620 AD into a noble Northumbrian family. At an early age, he began studies at the Lindisfarne Priory, where he became…

saints.name: Afterfeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.title: Afterfeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.notes: The second day of the Afterfeast of Theophany falls on January 8. At Vespers we repeat a hymn which has already been sung at Compline for Theophany. In the hymn Saint John wonders in whose name he should baptize Christ. Should he baptize Him in the name of the Father? The Lord Jesus Christ already…

saints.name: George the Chozebite
saints.title: Venerable George the Chozebite, Abbot
saints.notes: Saint George the Chozebite was born on the island of Cyprus toward the end of the sixth century. After the death of his parents, he went to Palestine to worship at the holy places. Here he entered into the monastic community of Chozeba between the River Jordan and Jerusalem, and he later became…

saints.name: Domnica of Constantinople
saints.title: Venerable Domnica of Constantinople
saints.notes: Saint Domnica came from Carthage to Constantinople in the time of the holy Emperor Theodosius the Great. Here she was baptized by Patriarch Nectarius and entered a women’s monastery. Through strict and prolonged ascetic effort she attained to high spiritual perfection. The saint healed the…

saints.name: Emilian the Confessor
saints.title: Saint Emilian the Confessor, Bishop of Cyzicus
saints.notes: Saint Emilian was a zealous defender of the holy icons during the reign of Emperor Leo the Armenian. He suffered torture and martyrdom in the year 820. His main feast is August 8.

saints.name: Gregory
saints.title: Venerable Gregory, Wonderworker of the Kiev Near Caves
saints.notes: Saint Gregory was tonsured at the Kiev Caves monastery in the time of Saint Theodosius (May 3). The saint devoted much time to reading books, which were his sole possession. He had the ability to bring thieves to their senses. Several times robbers broke in on him in his cell or in the garden, but…

saints.name: Gregory the Recluse
saints.title: Venerable Gregory the Recluse, of the Kiev Caves
saints.notes: Saint Gregory, Hermit of the Caves, lived during the fourteenth century. In the “Lives of the Saints Whose Relics lie in the Cave of Saint Theodosius,” it says that uncooked grass served as Saint Gregory’s food all his life. He gave this grass to those coming to him, and the sick…

saints.name: Isidore and 72 others at Yuriev
saints.title: Hieromartyr Isidore and 72 others at Yuriev, Estonia
saints.notes: Saint Isidore was priest of Saint Nicholas church in the city of Yuriev (Derpto, at present Taru in Estonia). According to the terms of a treaty concluded in 1463 between the Moscow Great Prince Ivan III and the Livonian knights, the latter were obligated to extend every protection to the Orthodox…

saints.name: Paisius of Uglich
saints.title: Saint Paisius of Uglich
saints.notes: Saint Paisius of Uglich was igumen of the Protection monastery, near Uglich. He was born in the Tver district near the city of Kashin, and he was a nephew of Saint Macarius of Kalyazin (March 17). Saint Paisius entered his uncle’s monastery after the death of his parents, when he was just an…

saints.name: Carterius of Caesarea in Cappadocia
saints.title: Saint Carterius of Caesarea in Cappadocia
saints.notes: Saint Carterius lived during the reign of Diocletian, and was a teacher in Caesarea of Cappadocia. He stood before a statue of Serapis and prayed to Christ, and the idol shattered to pieces. The procurator Urbanus ordered Saint Carterius to be tortured and then beheaded. Some, however, say he was…

saints.name: Martyrs Theophilus the Deacon
saints.title: Martyrs Theophilus the Deacon, and Helladius, in Libya
saints.notes: Saint Theophilus the deacon suffered with Saint Helladius. After confessing Christ before the governor of Libya, they were tortured and slain.

saints.name: Martyrs Julian and his wife
saints.title: Martyrs Julian and his wife, Basilissa, and those with them in Egypt
saints.notes: The Holy Martyr Julian was born in the Egyptian city of Antinoe, and to satisfy his parents he entered into marriage with the noble and rich maiden, Basilissa. Though married, the spouses remained virginal. Upon the death of their parents they built two monasteries: one for men, and one for women.…

saints.name: Elias the Hermit
saints.title: Venerable Elias the Hermit, of Egypt
saints.notes: Saint Elias the Egyptian became a monk and pursued asceticism for seventy-five years on a desolate mountain in a cave. He died in the fourth century at the age of 110.

saints.name: Abo the Perfumer
saints.title: Martyr Abo the Perfumer, of Tbilisi, Georgia
saints.notes: In the 8th century a Saracen army tyrannized Kartli as a first step towards overturning the Georgian nation. The invaders were certain that the best way to conquer Georgia was to uproot the Christian Faith. The Georgian people were alarmed, and the clergy and the best sons of Kartli sought…

saints.name: Gregory of Ochrid
saints.title: Venerable Gregory of Ochrid
saints.notes: Saint Gregory was a faithful teacher and shepherd of Christ’s flock. An inscription in the church of Holy Wisdom (Hagia Sophia) in Ochrid refers to him as “Gregory the Wise.”

saints.name: Afterfeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.title: Afterfeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.notes: The third day of the Afterfeast of Theophany falls on January 9. The hymns of this period invite us to purify our minds in order to see Christ.

saints.name: Polyeuktos of Melitene in Armenia
saints.title: Martyr Polyeuktos of Melitene in Armenia
saints.notes: Saint Polyeuktos1 (Polу́euktos) was the first to be martyred for Christ in the Armenian city of Melitene (Melitēnḗ). He was a soldier during the reign of Emperor Decius (249-251), and he later suffered martyrdom in the reign of Valerian (253-259). He was a friend of Nearkhos…

saints.name: Philip
saints.title: Hieromartyr Philip, Metropolitan of Moscow and All Russia
saints.notes: Saint Philip, Metropolitan of Moscow, in the world Theodore, was descended from the illustrious noble lineage of the Kolichevi, occupying a prominent place in the Boyar duma at the court of the Moscow sovereigns. He was born in the year 1507. His father, Stephen Ivanovich, “a man enlightened…

saints.name: Shemaiah
saints.title: Prophet Shemaiah (Samaia or Semeias)
saints.notes: The Prophet Shemaiah (Samaia) lived under King Solomon and his son Rehoboam. At that time, the kingdom of Israel in the north was divided from the southern kingdom of Juda. Israel was comprised of ten loosely united tribes, and Juda of two tribes. The prophet ordered Rehoboam not to make war…

saints.name: Peter
saints.title: Saint Peter, Bishop of Sebaste, in Armenia
saints.notes: Saint Peter, Bishop of Sebaste, was a brother of Saint Basil the Great and Saint Gregory of Nyssa (January 1 and January 10). His older sister, Saint Macrina (July 19) played a large role in his upbringing. Saint Basil the Great ordained Saint Peter as presbyter, and later he was made Bishop of…

saints.name: Eustratius the Wonderworker
saints.title: Saint Eustratius the Wonderworker
saints.notes: Saint Eustratius came from the city of Tarsus. At twenty years of age he secretly left his parents’ home and settled in the Abgar monastery (on Olympos in Asia Minor). There he lived a strict ascetic life, eating only bread and water, and spending his nights at prayer. After a certain while…

saints.name: Afterfeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.title: Afterfeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.notes: The fourth day of the Afterfeast of Theophany falls on January 10. Some of the hymns of this period compare the streams of the Jordan to the life-giving waters of Baptism.

saints.name: Gregory
saints.title: Saint Gregory, Bishop of Nyssa
saints.notes: Saint Gregory, Bishop of Nyssa, was a younger brother of Saint Basil the Great (January 1). His birth and upbringing came at a time when the Arian disputes were at their height. Having received an excellent education, he was at one time a teacher of rhetoric. In the year 372, he was consecrated by…

saints.name: Dometian
saints.title: Saint Dometian, Bishop of Melitene
saints.notes: Saint Dometian, Bishop of Melitene, was born and lived during the sixth century, in the time of the emperor Justin the Younger. He was married but was widowed, and thereafter he became a monk and lived a strict and holy life. At thirty years of age he was chosen bishop of the city of Melitene (in…

saints.name: Marcian the Presbyter in Constantinople
saints.title: Saint Marcian the Presbyter in Constantinople
saints.notes: Saint Marcian, Presbyter of the Great Church, was born at Rome and in his youth he received a first-rate education in Constantinople. After the death of his parents, Saint Marcian used his inheritance on the building, renovation and embellishment of churches. Thus, he built a church dedicated to…

saints.name: Paul
saints.title: Venerable Paul, Abbot of Obnora, Vologda
saints.notes: Saint Paul of Obnora, a famed disciple of Saint Sergius of Radonezh, was born at Moscow in the year 1317. From his youth he distinguished himself by his piety and kindliness towards the poor and suffering. His rich parents prepared him for a secular life, but at twenty-two years of age he secretly…

saints.name: Makarios of Pisma and Kostroma
saints.title: Venerable Makarios of Pisma and Kostroma

saints.title: Afterfeast of the Theophany of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ
saints.notes: The fifth day of the Afterfeast of Theophany falls on January 11. Many of the hymns of this period glorify Christ as God Who sanctifies the waters of Jordan by being baptized in them.

saints.name: Theodosius the Great

saints.notes: Saint Theodosius the Great lived during the fifth-sixth centuries, and was the founder of cenobitic monasticism. He was born in Cappadocia of pious parents. saints.notes: Saint Peter was slain at Hieropolis between 309—320 for confessing Christ.

saints.notes: Jeremiah I was Ecumenical Patriarch from 1522-1546, with one interruption in the year 1526. He was from Zitsa in Epirus, and was elected Metropolitan of Sofia before 1513. saints.name: Nino
saints.title: Saint Nino (Nina), Equal of the Apostles, Enlightener of Georgia
saints.notes: The virgin Nino of Cappadocia was a relative of Great-martyr George and the only daughter of a widely respected and honorable couple. saints.name: Joseph Analytinus of Raithu
saints.title: Saint Joseph Analytinus of Raithu
saints.notes: Saint Joseph Analytinus of Raithu was a strict ascetic. He attained such a high degree of perfection in the spiritual life that a light shone upon him while he prayed. He foretold the time of his death to his disciple Gelasius, and died in peace, before the slaughter of the Sinai Fathers.

saints.name: Theodulus
saints.title: Venerable Theodulus, son of Venerable Nilus of Sinai
saints.notes: Saint Theodulus was the son of Saint Nilus the Faster (November 12), and he recorded the slaughter of the holy Fathers at Raithu in the fifth century. saints.name: Stephen
saints.title: Venerable Stephen, Abbot of Khenolakkos Monastery, near Chalcedon
saints.notes: Saint Stephen lived during the eighth century, and was born into a family in Cappadocia, who raised him in great piety. As he reached maturity, he was greatly impressed by reading the lives of the holy ascetics, and so he visited many monasteries in Palestine in order to observe their way of life.…

saints.name: Kentigern
saints.title: Saint Kentigern, first Bishop of Glasgow, Scotland
saints.notes: Saint Kentigern was from Lothian (in Scotland), and may have been of royal blood. saints.title: Holy Empress Markianḗ
saints.notes: Saint Markianḗ was the wife of Emperor Justin I the Elder (reigned 518 - 527). She was distinguished for her piety, her ascetical life, and her philanthropy. Her righteous death was peaceful, and she was buried in the church of the Holy Apostles at Constantinople.

saints.notes: Saint Askiot reigned in Georgia in the IX century. This pious ruler built many churches as well as several monasteries. He was killed by Arabs in the church of the castle at Artanugi, Georgia, which he had built. In the Georgian Synaxaria it is also referred to as Kouropalatis.

saints.notes: Saint Ephraim the Syrian, a teacher of repentance, was born at the beginning of the fourth century in the city of Nisibis (Mesopotamia) into the family of impoverished toilers of the soil. saints.notes: Saint Illyricus the Wonderworker devoted himself to ascetic struggles on Mount Myrsinon in the Peloponnesus. The dates of his birth and death are unknown.

saints.name: Martyrs Elpidephorus
saints.title: Martyrs Elpidephorus, Dius, Bithonius, and Galycus
saints.notes: The Holy Martyrs Elpidephorus, Dius, Bithonius, and Galycus suffered for their faith in Jesus Christ. They cut off the head of Saint Elpidephorus with a sword, Saint Dius was executed by stoning, Saint Bithonius was drowned in the sea, and Saint Galycus was condemned to be eaten by wild beasts.

saints.title: “Unfading Flower” Icon of the Mother of God
saints.notes: The "Unfading Flower" Icon depicts the Theotokos holding her Divine Son on her right arm, and in her left hand is a bouquet of white lilies. saints.name: Joseph the Hymnographer
saints.title: Venerable Joseph the Hymnographer
saints.notes: Saint Joseph the Hymnographer, “the sweet-voiced nightingale of the Church,” was born in Sicily around the turn of the 9th century into a pious Christian family. saints.name: George of Mount Maleon in the Peloponnesus
saints.title: Venerable George of Mount Maleon in the Peloponnesus
saints.notes: Saint George lived during the ninth century. His parents arranged a marriage for him, but he refused to marry the woman they had chosen. He entered the monastery on Mount Maleon in the Peloponnesus, and many disciples gathered around him. He was able to see the future, and predicted his own death…

saints.name: Joseph the Much-Ailing
saints.title: Venerable Joseph the Much-Ailing, of the Kiev Far Caves
saints.notes: Saint Joseph the Much-Ailing lived during the fourteenth century. In his grievous illness he turned to God with prayer and vowed that if the Lord granted him health, he would then serve the brethren of the Kiev Caves monastery until the end of his days. saints.name: Zosimas
saints.title: Venerable Zosimas, Abbot of Vorbozomsk
saints.notes: Saint Zosimas of Vorbozomsk was the founder of a monastery dedicated to the Annuniciation of the Most Holy Theotokos on an island in Lake Vorbozoma, twenty-three versts south of White Lake. saints.name: Zosimas of Palestine
saints.title: Venerable Zosimas of Palestine
saints.notes: Saint Zosimas was born near the end of the fifth century, and lived in a monastery by the Jordan River. He met Saint Mary of Egypt (April 1), gave her Holy Communion, then buried her. Saint Zosimas lived to be one hundred years old, then fell asleep in the Lord around 560.

saints.notes: The Holy Martyr Pherbutha (Phermoutha) and her sister and servants were martyred for Christ between the years 341 and 343. saints.name: New Martyr Niketas of Pojani and Serres
saints.title: New Martyr Niketas of Pojani and Serres
saints.notes: The holy New Martyr Niketas (Nikḗtas) was a Slav from Albania, but we know nothing of his family or his early life. saints.name: Isidore
saints.title: Saint Isidore, Bishop of Seville
saints.notes: Saint Isidore was born in the middle of the sixth century, and was related to the Visigoth royal family who converted to Orthodoxy from Arianism during his lifetime. Saint Isidore was the brother of three saints: Saint Leander (February 27), Saint Fulgentius, and Saint Florentina. Orphaned at an…

saints.name: Theonas
saints.title: Venerable Theonas, Archbishop of Thessalonica
saints.notes: Saint Theonas was a disciple of Saint James of Kastoria (November 1), and lived at the beginning of the sixteenth century. saints.title: Saint George Mtsire of Georgia
saints.notes: No information available at this time.

saints.notes: The Holy Gerontissa Icon of the Mother of God is kept reverently in Pantokrator Monastery on the Holy Mountain. saints.name: The Life Giving Fountain of the Mother of God
saints.title: The Life Giving Fountain of the Mother of God
saints.notes: The appearance of the Mother of God to Emperor Leo Marcellus occurred on April 4, 450. saints.notes: At the beginning of the XIX century the remarkable ascetic Constantine Theodoulos was living as a monk on Mount Athos. saints.name: Martyrs Agathopodes the Deacon and Theodulus the Reader at Thessalonica
saints.title: Martyrs Agathopodes the Deacon and Theodulus the Reader at Thessalonica
saints.notes: The Holy Martyrs Agathopodes the Deacon and Theodulus the Reader lived in Thessalonica during the reign of the emperor Diocletian (284-305) and Maximian (284-305) and were among the church clergy. The holy Deacon Agathopodes was very old, and Saint Theodulus very young. Both distinguished…

saints.notes: Saint Publius lived a life of asceticism in the Egyptian desert during the reign of the emperor Julian the Apostate (361-363). saints.title: Saint Plato the Confessor of Studion
saints.notes: Saint Plato was born in the year 735 into a pious Christian family of the parents, Sergius and Euphemia. saints.title: Venerable Theodora of Thessalonica

saints.title: Icon of the Mother of God of Kasperov
saints.notes: The Kasperov Icon of the Most Holy Theotokos. Tradition says that this holy icon had been brought to Cherson from Transylvania by a Serb at the end of the sixteenth century. saints.name: Claudius and those with him
saints.title: Martyr Claudius and those with him
saints.notes: Saints Claudius, Diodoros, Victor, Victorinus, Pappios, Serapion, and Nikephoros are most probably the same saints who are commemorated on January 31. See their Life on that date.

saints.name: Hypomone
saints.title: Martyr Hypomone
saints.notes: Saint Hypomone (Αγία Υπομονή), who suffered during the pre-Nicene persecutions, is not mentioned in the Synaxaristes of Saint Νikόdēmos (July 14), nor in the printed Menaia, but she is mentioned in Vatican Codex 1104 f. 986, which contains her Service, composed by Saint Theophanes…

saints.title: 3rd Saturday of Great Lent: Memorial Saturday
saints.notes: Saturday is the day which the Church has set aside for the commemoration of faithful Orthodox Christians departed this life in the hope of resurrection to eternal life. saints.name: Eutychius
saints.title: Saint Eutychius, Patriarch of Constantinople
saints.notes: Saint Eutychius, Archbishop of Constantinople, was born in a village called “Divine” in the province of Phrygia. His father Alexander was a soldier, and his mother Synesia was the daughter of the priest Hesychius of Augustopolis. Saint Eutychius received the first rudiments of his…

saints.name: Methodius
saints.title: Saint Methodius, Equal of the Apostles, Archbishop of Moravia, Enlightener of the Slavs
saints.notes: Saint Methodius, Archbishop of Moravia, died on April 6 in the year 885. His Life is found on May 11, when he is commemorated with Saint Cyril, Teacher of the Slavs.

saints.name: Platonis of Nisibis
saints.title: Saint Platonis of Nisibis, Syria
saints.notes: At first Saint Platonis (Platonίs) was a deaconess, but later she withdrew into the Nisibian desert, where she founded a women’s monastery. saints.name: 120 Martyrs of Persia
saints.title: 120 Martyrs of Persia
saints.notes: The Holy 120 Martyrs suffered under the Persian emperor Sapor. They were taken into captivity during the reign of the Byzantine Emperor Constantios (337-361). saints.name: Martyrs Jeremiah and Presbyter Archilias
saints.title: Martyrs Jeremiah and Presbyter Archilias
saints.notes: The Holy Martyrs Jeremiah and the Priest Archilius (Alchimius) suffered martyrdom in the third century. Saint Gregory Dialogus (March 12) mentions them.

saints.name: Gregory the Byzantine
saints.title: Venerable Gregory the Byzantine
saints.notes: Saint Gregory was a native of Constantinople, and pursued an ascetic life on Mt. Athos in the Lavra of Saint Athanasius (July 5). He was the spiritual guide of Saint Gregory Palamas (November 14).

saints.name: Monastic Martyr Gennadios of Dionysiou on Mount Athos
saints.title: Monastic Martyr Gennadios of Dionysiou on Mount Athos
saints.notes: Saint Gennadios (Gennádios) was a monk in the Holy Monastery of Dionysiou on Mount Athos. One day, the Igoumen of the Monastery sent him to accompany the monks Boniface and Eudokimos (Eudókimos) to Constantinople so they could become martyrs. saints.name: 3rd Sunday of Great Lent: Veneration of the Cross
saints.title: 3rd Sunday of Great Lent: Veneration of the Cross
saints.notes: The Third Sunday of Lent is that of the Veneration of the Cross. saints.title: Saint George the Confessor, Bishop of Mytilene
saints.notes: Saint George, Metropolitan of Mytilene, from his youth led a monastic life, and was especially accomplished in the virtue of humility. saints.notes: The Holy Martyr Calliopius was born in Perge, Pamphylia of the pious woman Theoklia, wife of a renowned senator. Theoklia was childless for a long time. saints.name: Serapion of Egypt
saints.title: Venerable Serapion of Egypt
saints.notes: Saint Serapion lived during the fifth century in Egypt. He was called the linen cloth-wearer (Sindonite) since he wore only a coarse linen garb called a “sindon.” From his youth the monk lived like the birds of the air, without a shelter. saints.title: Apostle Herodion of the Seventy, and those with Him
saints.notes: Saints Herodion (Rodion), Agabus, Asyncritus, Rufus, Phlegon and Hermes were among the Seventy Apostles, chosen by Christ and sent out by Him to preach (Synaxis of the Seventy Apostles: January 4). saints.title: Saint Niphon, Bishop of Novgorod
saints.notes: Saint Niphon was a monk of the Kiev Caves Monastery, where he struggled in asceticism. saints.title: Venerable Rufus the Obedient of the Kiev Far Caves

saints.title: Martyr Pausilippus of Heraclea in Thrace
saints.notes: The Holy Martyr Pausilippus suffered under the emperor Hadrian (117-138). Denunced by the pagans, he was brought to trial before the emperor and staunchly declared himself a Christian. saints.title: Saint Celestine, Pope of Rome
saints.notes: Saint Celestine, Pope of Rome (422-432), a zealous champion of Orthodoxy, lived during the reign of the holy Emperor Theodosius the Younger (408-450). saints.title: “Spanish” Icon of the Mother of God

saints.title: Hieromartyr Desan, Bishop in Persia, and 272 others with him
saints.notes: The Holy Martyrs Bishop Desan, Presbyter Mariabus, Abdiesus, and 270 others were put to death under the Persian emperor Sapor II. Imprisoned, they refused to turn away from the Christian Faith. In their number also was the Martyr Ia, who is commemorated also on September 11.

saints.title: Martyr Terence and 40 others beheaded at Carthage

saints.title: Martyrs of the Kvabtakhevi Monastery in Georgia

saints.name: Pharmuthius the Anchorite of Egypt
saints.title: Venerable Pharmuthius the Anchorite of Egypt

saints.title: Afterfeast of the Dormition of the Mother of God

saints.notes: Saint Mark, also called John, (Acts 12:12), was a nephew of Saint Barnabas, and was Bishop of Apollonia (Col. 4:10). It was in the house of his mother Maria that the persecuted disciples found shelter after the Ascension of the Lord.

saints.title: Apostle Justus of the Seventy
saints.notes: Saint Justus, called Barsaba, a son of Saint Joseph the Betrothed, was chosen with Matthias to replace Judas. He was a bishop and died a martyr’s death at Eleutheropolis.

saints.notes: Saint Artemas was bishop of Lystra, Lycia. He died in peace.

saints.name: Rebecca
saints.title: Righteous Rebecca
saints.notes: Rebecca was the wife of the Old Testament Patriarch Isaac, and the mother of Jacob and Esau. She is mentioned in Genesis 22:23; Chapters 24-28; and Chapter 49:31. Saint Paul also mentions her (Romans 9:10).
